design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable FPGA top-level for an intelligent active-aerodynamics controller with a real firmware-visible MMIO control plane, bounded streaming request/response transport, validation, freshness checking, safety gating, timeout handling, sticky fault reporting, and sanitized actuator command generation.
design_summary.operating_model: Single synchronous clk domain with active-low synchronous rst_n. The top accepts firmware CSR/MMIO transactions, ingests bounded 128-bit command packets, validates structure and freshness using sequence/epoch information, enforces timeout and safety rules, clamps and optionally slews only otherwise-valid actuator commands, emits compact status/telemetry, and provides external model transport handshake signals with the mandated directionality. On invalid, stale, timed-out, malformed, reset, or fault conditions, actuator output validity is deasserted and the fault is latched for software handling; no substitute command is generated.
external_interfaces: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO: csr_addr, csr_wdata, csr_valid, csr_write, csr_ready, csr_rdata, csr_rvalid.
Streaming command/status: cmd_in_valid, cmd_in_ready, cmd_in_data[127:0], status_out_valid, status_out_ready, status_out_data[63:0].
External model transport: model_request_valid/model_request_data outputs, model_request_ready input, model_response_valid/model_response_data inputs, model_response_ready output.
Actuator and fault outputs: actuator_cmd_valid, actuator_cmd_data[31:0], fault_irq.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Synthesizable top-level integration point for firmware control, streaming decode, safety conditioning, status generation, and fault reporting.
responsibilities: Provide the sole synthesizable top-level integration point.
Implement firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control and status access.
Decode and validate command packet fields.
Track sequence/epoch freshness and enforce timeout policy.
Reject malformed, stale, or discontinuous commands.
Clamp actuator commands to programmable min/max limits.
Optionally apply simple slew limiting when enabled.
Emit status/telemetry and fault interrupt indications.
Deassert actuator command validity on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions.
Provide external model request/response transport signals with the mandated directionality.
interface_notes: Top-level ports are fixed and must not be renamed or repurposed.

The external model transport follows the mandatory direction contract: model_request_valid/model_request_data are outputs, model_request_ready is an input, model_response_valid/model_response_data are inputs, and model_response_ready is an output.
Top-level outputs require real RTL drivers and are not left to child-input-only connectivity.
The top-level streaming bus width remains bounded at 128 bits.
ownership_notes: CSR/MMIO configuration and telemetry semantics are owned by adaptive_aero_control_csr_mmio.
Command decode, packet validation, freshness observation, and status packet formatting are owned by adaptive_aero_control_transport.
Actuator gating, clamp/slew conditioning, sticky fault behavior, and sanitized command validity are owned by adaptive_aero_control_safety_fsm.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_csr_mmio
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO register block and software-facing status collector.
responsibilities: Decode CSR address, write, and read transactions.
Expose readable control/status registers and their fields.
Drive configuration semantics into the controller as explicit outputs.
Provide readback and response timing through csr_ready/csr_rvalid.
Latch and report status/fault indications from the controller.
Ensure every declared register is reachable through RTL decode.
Publish freshness reference sequence and epoch values for downstream monitoring.
interface_notes: This is the real firmware-visible control plane required by the product journey.
The declared registers are CTRL, TIMEOUT_LIMIT, CLAMP_MIN, CLAMP_MAX, SLEW_LIMIT, STATUS, and TELEMETRY.
Software-visible state must be reachable through explicit address decode; inaccessible internal state is not described as software-visible.
The command packet input may be observed for diagnostics, but it does not replace the streaming transport.
ownership_notes: Owns cfg_timeout_limit, cfg_min_cmd, cfg_max_cmd, cfg_mode_enable, cfg_slew_enable, cfg_slew_limit, and cfg_fault_ack.
Owns csr_ready, csr_rdata, csr_rvalid, status_out_data, fresh_seq_current, and fresh_epoch_current.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_transport
module_architecture.role: Streaming transport and packet decode/format block.
responsibilities: Capture and decode the incoming 128-bit command packet.
Validate packet fields and produce explicit semantic outputs.
Track freshness, sequence continuity, epoch tags, and stale conditions.
Generate a compact status/telemetry packet.
Implement external model request/response handshake directionality.
Avoid any bulk FIFO or payload array buffering.
interface_notes: Packet fields include command_valid, command_mode, sequence, epoch, age tag, host acknowledgment, actuator target, checksum indication, malformed indication, and stale indication.
The external model transport is bounded and follows the mandatory direction contract.
The module does not infer tensors, geometry arrays, flow fields, or any surrogate model artifacts.
ownership_notes: Owns cmd_in_ready, model_request_valid, model_request_data, model_response_ready, and the packet decode outputs pkt_command_valid, pkt_command_mode, pkt_sequence, pkt_epoch, pkt_age_tag, pkt_host_ack, pkt_target_cmd, pkt_checksum_ok, pkt_malformed, pkt_stale.
Owns status_out_valid and status_out_data for the streaming status path.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety_fsm
responsibilities: Maintain safe active/inhibit state machine.
Gate actuator validity based on command validation and freshness.
Clamp commands to min/max bounds.
Optionally apply simple slew limiting when enabled.
Latch sticky fault status for software handling.
Report acceptance/rejection cause and current safety context.
Ensure no substitute command is driven on error conditions.
interface_notes: Only validated, fresh, non-stale packets may produce a valid actuator command.
Timeout, sequence discontinuity, malformed packet, or explicit fault deasserts validity and latches fault status.
Slew limiting may reduce per-cycle delta only for otherwise valid commands; it does not create validity.
No fallback command, fallback register, fallback controller, substitute command, or fallback-on-reset behavior is permitted.
ownership_notes: Owns status_accept_code, status_stale_flag, status_watchdog_expired, status_inhibit_flag, status_clamp_applied, status_current_mode, status_last_sequence, and status_sticky_fault.

interface_summary.intent: Expose the firmware-visible MMIO control plane and readable status snapshot.
Accept streaming command packets, generate status packets, and mediate external model transport with mandated directionality.
Apply controller configuration and decoded packet semantics to safety gating, clamping, and sticky-fault handling.
Provide firmware-controlled configuration and sticky-fault acknowledge to the safety FSM.
Supply validated packet semantics and error indications to the safety FSM.
Return safety status and sticky-fault context for readable firmware telemetry.
Drive the top-level streaming handshakes and telemetry outputs with real RTL sources.
Provide sanitized actuator command outputs and the fault condition used to drive the top-level fault interrupt.

data_flow_summary: Firmware writes CTRL, TIMEOUT_LIMIT, CLAMP_MIN, CLAMP_MAX, and SLEW_LIMIT through the CSR/MMIO block; the decoded control outputs are forwarded to the safety FSM.
A 128-bit command packet enters the transport block through cmd_in_valid/cmd_in_ready/cmd_in_data and is decoded into semantic packet fields for downstream use.
The transport block tracks freshness using the current sequence and epoch references from the CSR/MMIO block and flags stale or malformed packets.
The safety FSM consumes the decoded packet fields, validates them against mode enable, timeout, freshness, and sequence rules, and only then may assert actuator_cmd_valid.

When valid, the safety FSM clamps actuator_cmd_data to configured min/max bounds and may optionally apply slew limiting if enabled; invalid conditions inhibit output validity rather than substituting a command.
Status information is generated as a compact 64-bit status packet by the transport block and mirrored through the CSR/MMIO block for firmware readback.
Sticky fault state is reported to firmware through STATUS/TELEMETRY and to the top-level fault_irq output.
External model transport is present as a bounded handshake path with request outputs and response inputs, but it does not replace the control or actuator path.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All sequential logic is synchronous to clk at 50.0 MHz with a 20 ns period. The design uses a single clock domain.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low and synchronous. On reset assertion, control registers return to documented defaults, packet decode outputs clear, status outputs idle, model_request_valid is deasserted, model_response_ready follows the defined idle handshake behavior, actuator_cmd_valid is deasserted, sticky fault state clears, and no substitute command is generated. After reset release, the controller remains idle until a validated command is accepted.

integration_notes: The architecture is descriptive only and preserves the exact module names, port names, and filenames from the source specification.
The firmware-visible MMIO control plane is real and explicit; no declared register is treated as inaccessible internal state.

The external model transport direction contract takes precedence over ambiguous ingress/egress prose: request valid/data are outputs, request ready is an input, response valid/data are inputs, and response ready is an output.
Actuator outputs are sanitized before use, and invalid conditions inhibit validity rather than replacing commands.
No surrogate model, tensor handling, geometry arrays, pressure fields, flow fields, GPU dependency, or bulk flip-flop payload buffering is implied.
Any explicit history/FIFO storage, if ever needed, is described only through technology-neutral memory wrappers suitable for FPGA block RAM mapping.
The design uses no Sky130 macros.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
